articleTitle: A New Single-Phase High Gain Microinverter for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) microinverters have been a trending research area due to their modularity, plug-and-play capability, and ability to maximize power extraction from individual PV modules. This article introduces a new non-isolated, single-stage, single-phase high-gain microinverter for PV applications. The proposed microinverter, with its high gain capability, can interface a 35 V DC source with a 230 V AC grid. The topology comprises five switches, with one switch always operating at high frequency and the others operating at high frequency either during a positive half cycle or during a negative half cycle of the output voltage. The proposed microinverter is designed to achieve high voltage gain while operating in continuous conduction mode, and the topology also features dual grounding, resulting in negligible leakage current. The performance of the proposed high-gain microinverter is verified at a 300 W power rating using the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: A Coordinated Operation Control of Grid-forming and Grid-following to Improve Microgrid Large Signal Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: With the increasing prevalence of power electron-ics converters (PECs), large signal stability issues are rising, particularly in islanded microgrids (MGs). To maintain stable performance and cost-effective operation, MGs combine grid-forming (GFM) and grid-following (GFL) controls to achieve these objectives. This paper proposes a sophisticated coordinated operation control strategy for PECs, which dynamically switches between GFL and GFM control modes to enhance large signal stability in MGs. Unlike conventional approaches that trip PECs during fault conditions, the proposed method leverages coordinated GFM and GFL control to maintain continuous operation and stability during fault events. In order to show the effectiveness of the proposed coordinated operation control, numerical Simulink simulations are applied to islanded MG. The results show that the proposed control allows PEC to ride through the fault, ensure stable operation, and avoid unnecessary protection tripping.

articleTitle: A 12.11 mW, 99 pJ/Conv.-Step SAR ADC with Optimal Power Efficiency for IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This brief presents a capacitive charge scaling DAC architecture with a two-phase non-overlapping clocking scheme to make an energy-efficient Successive Approximation Register (SAR) data converter for Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications. The proposed architecture comprises a Track & Hold (T/H), a Modified Strong Arm Latch comparator (MSAL), a SAR Control logic, and a digital-to-analog (D/A) converter. The proposed work is simulated using Cadence Virtuoso in TSMC 180 nm and achieves a minimum sampling rate of 1 MS/s and power consumption of 12.11 mW. To address the effects of process variations and mismatches on ADC performance, this paper conducts a thorough 500-point Monte Carlo (MC) simulation of the proposed SAR ADC circuit. The measured results show a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 47.81 dB, a Spurious-Free Dynamic Range (SFDR) of 54.32 dB, and ENOB of 7.65 Bits.

articleTitle: Dual-port Output Non-isolated DC/DC Converter with Adaptive Inductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: In this paper, a non-isolated DC/DC converter with negative polarity input and two-port output is researched and designed based on the power amplifier (PA) in the RF front-end module of 5G communication. The converter is based on the traditional Buck-Boost converter with device-multiplexed two-port output, and an adaptive inductor is proposed, whose inductance value can be changed within a certain range with the change of current, which in turn improves the port voltage control flexibility. The article presents a modal analysis of the proposed converter and proposes an adaptive inductor to optimize the circuit. The principle of the adaptive inductor is analyzed and the correctness of the aforementioned analysis is verified by magnetic simulation and circuit simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Efficient Vehicle-to-Vehicle Wireless Power Transfer Using SPMC with Integrated APF for Enhanced Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) wireless power transfer (WPT) utilizing a Single-Phase Matrix Converter (SPMC). The SPMC efficiently performs both DC to AC and AC to DC conversion in the V2V WPT system. In the proposed system, the DC supply from the first vehicle is converted to high-frequency AC power using an SPMC. This high-frequency AC power is then transmitted wirelessly via inductive coupling between the transmitter coil in the first vehicle and the receiver coil in the second vehicle. Upon reception, the high-frequency AC power is converted back to DC power by another SPMC in the second vehicle to charge its battery. Additionally, during AC to DC conversion, the SPMC functions as an Active Power Filter (APF), significantly improving the power factor and power quality by reducing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in the supply current waveform to comply with IEEE-519 2022 standard. The proposed technique is modeled and simulated using MATLAB/Simulink, with selected results provided to validate the effectiveness of the approach. The findings demonstrate the SPMC's capability to enhance the efficiency and reliability of V2V WPT systems, providing a viable solution for the next generation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Analyzing Fault Tolerance in a 1.3 kw Six-Phase Fully Coreless Axial-Flux Permanent-Magnet Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The importance of fault-tolerant machines is growing rapidly as the electrical machine industry demands uninterrupted operational service in the context of the Fourth Industrial Revolution. Additionally, coreless axial-flux permanent-magnet (AFPM) machines have emerged as efficient solutions for power generation in recent industries, offering advantages such as reduced eddy current losses and cogging torque, thereby improving overall efficiency. This design supports high power density, particularly in fully coreless configurations. However, challenges like high leakage flux and reduced structural integrity hinder the widespread adoption of coreless AFPM machines. Moreover, integrating multi-phase setups in AFPM machines is more complex than in radial-flux permanent-magnet (RFPM) machines, as it requires more winding coils and increases the stator diameter, resulting in bulkier designs. This article emphasizes the fault tolerance performance of a 1.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{kW}$</tex> lightweight, fully coreless six-phase AFPM generator for small-scale power generation. To achieve this, a six-phase multi-stage AFPM generator was designed and simulated using ANSYS Maxwell®. Subsequently, a laboratory-scale prototype was fabricated accordingly. Three types of winding configurations were applied to the six-phase machine to evaluate the fault tolerance performance of each type. The fault tolerance performance was found to closely align with that of a referenced RFPM machine. Notably, the fully coreless six-phase machine demonstrated a significant power density of 205 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{W}/\mathbf{kg}$</tex>, along with high fault-tolerant capacity.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Electrical Performance of Single-Electrode Mode Triboelectric Nanogenerators Based on Different Conductor Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) have received a lot of interest in recent years as a potential solution to the global energy issue, due to their ability to efficiently convert various types of mechanical energy from the environment into usable electrical energy. Compared to the traditional energy harvesting methods, triboelectric nanogenerators offer advantages for self-powered devices. This study investigates the electrical performance of triboelectric nanogenerators in single-electrode mode (SE-TENGs) with different conductor materials, including copper and aluminum with fixed dielectric material. The operating mechanism of the fabricated TENGs is based on contact and separation by manual hand tapping. The selected materials are assessed based on performance criteria such as output voltage, current, output power density, cost, and environmental impact. The output voltage and current were measured using the digital multimeter and oscilloscope with a frequency oscillation of 2 Hz. As a result, the PTFE configuration with the copper foil was able to generate a high voltage of up to 78.8 V and a current of 1.2 µA. The results show that the choice of conductor materials can be used effectively in various applications, from wearable electronics to large-scale energy harvesting, and providing a balanced approach to performance and economic feasibility. These findings provide valuable insights for the optimization and design of triboelectric nanogenerators in energy harvesting applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Teager Energy in Time Frequency Transforms with a Concentrated Discrete Window
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The time frequency representation (TFR) of a signal offers extensive details regarding the local spectrum at specific time instants. However, a notable drawback of the linear time frequency transforms (TFT) is that it is challenging to obtain high resolution in both time and frequency simultaneously due to the Heisenberg's ambiguity principle. This limitation hampers the effectiveness of linear TFTs in accurately determining the temporal components of a signal, and detecting finite duration events. To address this issue, a modified version of the linear TFTs, incorporating the proposed Teager energy concentrated discrete window (TECDW) based on the optimized discrete Teager energy concentration (DTEC) measure is suggested. This method is especially advantageous for accurately identifying specific finite duration events embedded in noise, and precisely identifying the start and end of such events. The simulated outcomes indicate that the proposed approach can effectively distinguish signal components in the time domain while attaining the highest DTEC in the frequency domain.

articleTitle: Feedback Control of Printing Nozzle by Force Sensing Device with High-accuracy Load Cell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Many of the deposition-based 3D printing technologies work on a predetermined path, which makes it difficult to respond to changes in the layering surfaces. The purpose of this study is to realize a layering motion that maintains a constant pressing force even when the surface to be layered is not flat by measuring the reaction force applied to the nozzle during the layering process and feedback them. By installing a high-accuracy load cell at the base of the nozzle, the vertical reaction forces and moments applied to the nozzle are acquired in real-time. In this paper, we describe a force measurement device using a high-accuracy load cell to measure reaction forces during printing. A feedback system was developed to control the nozzle motion based on the nozzle reaction force. Experiments were conducted on two slope patterns to verify the followability of the nozzle on sloped surfaces. The results of the experiment showed that the printing was achieved by maintaining the pressing force and cross-sectional shape suitable for layering in response to changes in the printing basement.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Brain Source Localization of Mental Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Workplace demands and pressures often lead to mental stress, affecting productivity and well-being. In parallel, in neuroscience and clinical research, the precise localization of the brain source activity using electroencephalography (EEG) data is of significant importance. This paper focuses on utilizing EEG data collected from volunteers consisting of administrative assistants and staff at the American University of Sharjah to localize brain sources while performing the Stroop Color Word Test mental task. We employ the source affine image reconstruction algorithm to analyze the data. Stress induction is achieved through time. Source localization was also performed during stress mitigation using 16 Hz Binaural Beats (BBs). Our findings reveal that mental stress predominantly appears in the frontal lobe of the brain and demonstrates the potential of BBs in mitigating stress levels.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Switched-Capacitor Common-Grounded Multilevel Inverter for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the performance of induction motor (IM) drives by implementing a three-phase switched-capacitor Common-Grounded multilevel inverter (TCGMLI) for speed control. Transformerless multilevel inverters (TMIs) are increasingly preferred for electric vehicle applications due to their superior output quality and step-up capabilities without the need for transformers. However, existing TMIs often necessitate additional components to achieve high step-up outputs. To overcome this limitation, a seven-level (7L) switched capacitor (SC) TMI with a common-ground feature. This design incorporates a soft-charging resonant cell to minimize inrush current. Achieving low total harmonic distortion (THD) and precise speed regulation of the induction motor is facilitated by maintaining a constant (V/f) ratio and managing slip speed. A proportional-integral (PI) controller is employed to stabilize the motor speed. The closed-loop system's performance is evaluated under various scenarios, including changes in reference speed, dynamic loads, and speed disturbances. The paper presents a comparative analysis of the performance and efficiency o f an IM drive using v/f control versus a closed-loop TSCMLI system. Simulation results, obtained using MATLAB/SIMULINK, validate the effectiveness of the proposed system in improving motor drive performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: Enhancing System Resilience: MILP Application for Efficient Load Reduction in Islanded Multi-Area Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Power utilities have prioritized the integration of Distributed Generation (DG), particularly from renewable energy sources. The decentralized control approach has allowed utilities to operate the DGs in islanding mode in order to maximize energy potential. Nevertheless, the operation of an islanding system presents substantial obstacles to system stability, necessitating the implementation of additional load management (load shedding) controls to preserve the energy balance. Load shedding techniques are implemented to alleviate this issue and stabilize the system. Traditional methods (often sequential) fail to account for load priority and extreme contingencies, resulting in either excessive/inadequate reduction or the potential disconnection of critical loads. This paper proposes a load reduction strategy that is effective for islanded multi-area distribution systems. It utilizes Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) optimization to ascertain the optimal load combination for shedding, taking into account load priorities (vital, non-vital, and semi-vital). The efficacy of the proposed method is verified through simulations on a modified multi-area system that consists of three identical IEEE 13 bus systems. The approach demonstrates superior performance in rapidly stabilizing the system by ensuring power supply for critical loads. This methodology improves the sustainability of the system by decreasing the number of load sheds, optimizing the power supply for critical loads, and surpassing the efficacy of current adaptive techniques.

articleTitle: Vulnerability of Demand Response Programs under Price Anticipating and Cooperative Agent Behaviour
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Demand Response (DR) is instrumental in shifting the peak demand and effectively handling the variability of deep renewable energy penetration in the power grid. Price-based demand response programs have been proposed by researchers as an important tool. In this work, we first discuss that strategic price-anticipating human behavior can adversely affect the efficiency of price-based demand response. Next, we show that if the strategic price anticipating agents cooperate with others, the social welfare can reduce further. The situation is modeled using coalitional game. Under some conditions on utility functions, the modeled cooperative game can be superadditive and the payoff allocation is in the core. Thus, strategic agents can make stable and profitable coalitions resulting more damage to efficiency. So, while designing price signal, the impact of agent behavior needs to be analyzed carefully for achieving efficient performance.

articleTitle: Mission-Profile Based Reliability Assessment of Grid Integrated Photovoltaic System Installed in the United Arab Emirates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The reliability of power electronic converters in a photovoltaic system has become major concern to extend its power transfer capability. In this regard, this work conducts a mission-profile-based reliability assessment of a 6-kW, two-stage, grid-integrated photovoltaic system installed in the United Arab Emirates. This study considers the failure of power switches in the dc-dc (boost) converter and dc-ac inverter, and the failure of the dc-link capacitor. This investigation uncovered that the dc-link capacitor exhibits the highest susceptibility to failure within the system, with the switches of the dc-dc converter and PV inverter following closely behind. Overall, the PV system has a B10 lifetime of 09 years in UAE. However, the overall lifetime of the system can be improved further by applying various control strategies to manage the thermal load of the power devices.

articleTitle: Research on a Negative Non-isolated Multi-port DC-DC Converter Based on LC Resonant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The birth of the fifth generation wireless communication technology marks a significant increase in data transmission speed, a significant reduction in latency, and a significant increase in device connectivity. In order to meet the traffic needs of 5G and MIMO, this project studies a DC/DC converter with negative polarity single input and positive polarity multiple output based on this background. The main focus of this project is to establish a new topology structure of an LC resonant negative polarity single input positive polarity multiple output non isolated converter. This topology structure is based on the four-switch Buck-Boost (FSBB) converter, replacing the switch in the FSBB with a diode, simplifying the two-port output circuit topology, and using single output as the main analysis point, conducting modal analysis, circuit characteristic analysis. The analysis is verified using simulation experiment.

articleTitle: R-TAP: A Cloud-Based Multi-Region Road Traffic Accident Severity Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The tremendous impact of road traffic accidents (RTAs) remains a global concern, especially in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). While most LMICs have limited budget to afford advanced traffic monitoring systems, it is necessary to develop feasible solutions for enhancing road safety in these regions. Recent studies have extensively explored the applicability of machine learning (ML) models to predict RTA severity in different regions. However, there is limited exploration of training and evaluating the performance of ML model from a multi-region perspective. Further investigation is also necessary to formulate a cost-effective implementation strategy for LMICs to deploy ML models for real-time prediction. Hence, this paper contributes by proposing R-TAP, which deploys a TabNet-based model on the cloud for multi-region RTA severity predictions. A web application is also developed to receive inputs and visualise the prediction results. The TabNet model is trained on a multi-region dataset consisting of 42 features, produced by combining the individual RTA datasets collected from Australia, Brazil, Ethiopia, New Zealand, the UK, and the US. Evaluation with random forest and multinomial logistic regression showed that TabNet can achieve performance comparable to random forest. It also has the highest area under the receiver operating characteristics at 0.8857. R-TAP is also simulated using testing samples as real-time input, with an overall execution time of 4.104s per prediction. It is considered satisfactory and is expected to be useful for emergency responders to make informed decisions. This solution is expected to support LMICs in their roadmap towards enhanced road safety. Future research is essential to improve the predictive power and include datasets from more regions for a more inclusive RTA severity prediction.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Management System for Green Hydrogen Production and Seawater Desalination Plants with Demand Response Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper presents an optimal Energy Management System (EMS) of a grid-connected green Hydrogen Production Plant (HPP) and Seawater Reverse Osmosis (SWRO) desalination plant. The proposed EMS integrates the HPP with a SWRO desalination plant to optimally supply the water to the HPP electrolysis while meeting the desired hydrogen, water, and electrical demands. The objective of the EMS is to minimize the energy costs associated with the grid interaction and contribute to Demand Response (DR) programs. The optimization problem is formulated and solved using a MATLAB optimization toolbox. The results demonstrated the purchase of energy during low electricity tariff periods. Contributing to the demand response programs results in a decrease in the operational cost by 1.4-2.5%. The results also showed that the desalinated water used for hydrogen production incurs a negligible energy consumption, comprising only 0.0576% of the electrolyzer's total energy usage.

articleTitle: Energy Generating from Footsteps on Piezoelectric Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Energy harvesting has become a compelling area of research, especially as the global community seeks green alternatives for energy generation. This paper suggests the construction of an energy harvester prototype and its voltage and current output, along with the optimization process for maximizing power output from a piezoelectric tile. Electric energy generation, when a load is applied to sensors, either through direct strain or ambient vibrations-depends on various factors, including the number of piezoelectric transducers, the electromechanical coupling coefficient of the sensors, the applied load, and the arrangement scheme. A prototype piezoelectric floor tile 1 by 1 feet was developed to evaluate its energy harvesting potential, recording and analyzing the energy generated. Two experiment types were conducted to assess harvesting performance: one focused on connection configurations and the other on external factors. The energy harvester floor tile incorporated low-grade piezoelectric diaphragms, like those in buzzers. Results showed that the series connection produced the lowest voltage, but higher current compared to the parallel connection achieved the highest voltage but with lower current output at 0.011mA. The result also shows running produced slightly higher voltage compared to walking.

articleTitle: Machine Parameters Estimation Using Closed-Loop Control Signal Curve Fitting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Apart from the current limits, the voltage limits will also affect the achievable performance of a motor drive. The voltage limits for a fault-tolerant drive will decide the maximum operating speed of the machine before flux weakening, hence the maximum attainable output power. Unlike current limits, the voltage limits of the fault-tolerant drive depend on the machine parameters. Hence, an accurate machine parameter needs to be obtained to estimate the voltage variations under different fault scenarios. By using the measured currents and plugging it into the machine voltage equations, the theoretical voltages for the machine can be calculated using some initial values for the machine parameters. Accurate machine parameters can be obtained by optimizing the machine parameters to minimize the theoretical voltage and the actual control voltages. It is shown that the estimated machine parameters are accurate enough to predict the control voltage references under varying operating conditions.

articleTitle: A Single-Stage Single-Phase Boost Inverter with Common Ground and Continuous Input Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: In this paper, a single-stage boost inverter is proposed to be used in low voltage input photovoltaic applications. It improves upon a novel non-isolated integrated boost inverter topology by increasing the voltage levels from two to three, enabling zero-voltage generation and achieving continuous input current. The proposed topology allows for zero current leakage by establishing a shared ground between input and AC output. Another benefit of the proposed inverter is that a proposed modulation is used to reduce input current amplitude and stress. The working principle and analysis of the proposed inverter are elaborated. The modelling of the proposed topology is established in MATLAB/Simulink. Finally, the simulation and experimental results confirm the validity of the proposed inverter concept.

articleTitle: The Study of Overlaid Noise and Modeling for Two Onboard DC/DC Converters with Relative Positions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Power semiconductor switching in converters enables equipment miniaturization, leading to increased instances of multiple converters operating nearby. This results in more electromagnetic noise sources and conduction noise overlay, exacerbating electromagnetic interference and necessitating a reassessment of noise mitigation strategies. A valuable approach involves designing noise-reducing filters through simulation, offering a simplified yet accurate method. This study evaluates noise overlay from the positioning of multiple power converters, demonstrating the effectiveness of proposed simulation-based modeling considering noise overlay from the positioning.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Camera Sensor for Helmet Detection in Two-Wheelers and Its Integration with the Electronic Control Unit (ECU)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The governing bodies set across different regions have several rules and regulations for the safety of motorcyclists, which they must adhere to. Accidents are undesirable events that result in injuries, or sometimes even worse, deaths. These accidents could be averted by wearing helmets while riding. The idea of integrating the output of the image processing algorithms with the ignition system stems from the increased fatality rate of motorcyclists on the road. Therefore, this project aims to reduce such accidents by using a camera tracker as a sensor, where it is further implemented with image processing hardware, such as the Raspberry Pi Camera Module, which runs image processing algorithm to determine if helmet is being worn by the rider or not. Furthermore, Raspberry Pi Camera Module is connected to the ECU using appropriate communication protocols, and the ECU sends outputs that control the ignition system. For the helmet detection, control logics on microcontroller are developed in a way to send signals to the ECU regarding helmet detection status. This project is focused on improving safety and reducing accidents.

articleTitle: Multilevel Converter-Based Charging Station for A Fleet of Electric Transit Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper introduces the idea of a multilevel converter-based charging station specifically designed for a fleet of electric buses. The proposed approach uses a cascaded H-bridge (CHB) converter as an active front-end rectifier to draw power from an ac grid. Each electric bus is connected to the dc link of the CHB cell and is equipped with an on-board charger based on a modular multilevel converter (MMC). The battery bank of each electric bus is divided among the submodules (SMs) of an on-board MMC, which can charge the battery bank as well as supply power to the electric drive. An electric bus fleet can be a backup during emergencies and provide support by feeding power into the ac grid as part of ancillary services. This paper presents the bidirectional power flow of the multilevel charging station for this purpose. The simulation results, and analysis of the combined operation of CHB and MMC to charge the battery bank of an electric bus are presented to verify the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Cogging Torque Reduction Using Magnet Phase Inverted Shape in Dual Axial Gap Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper describes the design of permanent magnets for dual axial gap motors to reduce cogging torque. In this method, a radially segmented and circumferentially shifted skewed shape is designed and placed in the lower part of the rotor axial direction. The phase inverted shape, which is designed by inverted the phase of the skewed shape with respect to the central axis, is placed in the upper part of the rotor axial direction. This cancels the cogging torque waveforms generated in the upper and lower axial directions. Furthermore, the magnet shape was optimized to maximize the cancel effect. First, the cogging torque waveform was predicted from the magnet shape, and then a shape was selected that satisfied the cancelable conditions and analyzed using 3DFEM. As a result, a magnet shape that reduces cogging torque by 94.6% was obtained.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Advancements in Battery Charger Technologies for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) necessitates significant advancements in battery charger technologies to enhance efficiency, reliability, and integration with existing infrastructure. This paper offers a comprehensive review of current and future battery charger technologies for EVs, focusing on AC/DC and DC/DC converter topologies, bidirectional charging systems, and inductive charging solutions. AC/DC converters, such as bridgeless power factor correction circuits, and DC/DC converters, including boost and multilevel converters, are evaluated for their efficiency, control complexity, and thermal management. Recent innovations like the Multi-device Interleaved DC-DC Bidirectional Converter (MDIBC) and integrated onboard chargers (iOBCs) are highlighted for improving power density and compactness. Bidirectional charging, including Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) and Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) applications, provides flexible energy storage and grid stability. Challenges in managing bidirectional power flow, battery longevity, and grid integration are addressed with advanced control strategies and innovative converter designs. Inductive charging, or wireless power transfer (WPT), eliminates physical connectors and supports dynamic charging scenarios. The review covers enhancements in power transfer efficiency, alignment mechanisms, and control strategies, such as three-coil inductive power transfer systems and multistage constant current charging profiles. This review emphasizes the importance of advanced battery charger technologies for the sustainable growth of the EV industry, highlighting ongoing research and development to improve efficiency and integration in electric transportation infrastructure.

articleTitle: Stress Pattern Recognition Using Spatio Temporal Features Based on EEG Sport Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Several emotional factors that can induce stress affect participants performance during the competition, such as choking under pressure. This study aims to evaluate the performance of golf players under psychological pressure by creating a scenario in a golf putting simulation test. We forced each participant to compete by making a monetary reward scenario based on their winning score to increase each participant's stress level. Their winning score is classified as poor or good by measuring the distance to the target achievement. The objective is to detect the stress pattern by observing the prominent features and window segments in the alpha band. Our approach is processing the EEG data by wavelet transform and extracting the data into spatio temporal features in the central and occipital lobe. Our investigation found that the maximum amplitude and band power feature values were higher when the participants performed well, and this pattern is reversed when the participant's performance is poor. Meanwhile, based on brain area activity in a good performance, we found that central area activity is high from the first to the fourth segment. In contrast, occipital area activity is high only until the third segment. Following these parts, brain activity decreases compared to its previous state. This study also discovered that the significant segment window is located in the tenth segment, with a P-value < 0.05 between good and poor performance. Thus, this analysis's results can be used to recommend neurofeedback training for athletes to prevent choking under pressure.

articleTitle: Fault Identification Technique to Identify Open Circuit Fault Switch Location Based on SPMC Boost Rectifier Circuit Using MATLAB Simulink
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive fault identification technique for a single-phase matrix converter (SPMC) based boost rectifier circuit. The primary objective of the fault identification technique is to identify the faulty switch during an open circuit fault (OCF) using diagnostic techniques monitoring the input supply's cycle, the output voltage, and the inductor current magnitude as well as the current and voltage measurement to obtain the binary code. To interpret the fault occurrence, a binary code is created to interpret the faulty switch, which serves as a signal to a controller to initiate the appropriate Current Option Route (COR) strategy. This configuration is intended to reroute current to operational switches in the condition of an Open Circuit Fault (OCF) and maintain the necessary current direction in the circuit. Using MATLAB Simulink, the switching operation of the COR approach and fault identification technique is presented. The successful generation and application of the binary code for fault identification and correction highlight the robustness and practical utility of the proposed method in enhancing the reliability of the SPMC-based boost rectifier system.

articleTitle: A Multi-Functional Virtual Impedance for Droop-Controlled Inverter-Based Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: In isolated microgrids, conventional droop control was introduced to attain equal power sharing while maintaining voltage and system frequency. However, the conventional droop control leads to poor reactive power sharing because of the microgrid feeders mismatch. To tackle this issue, the virtual impedance was proposed to improve the accuracy of reactive power sharing by eliminating the effect of the mismatch in microgrid feeders. On the other side, the virtual impedance was employed for other purposes such as limiting the DG output current during faults to increase the sensitivity of the protection system. Utilizing the virtual impedance for achieving the reactive power sharing enhancement and increasing the protection system sensitivity in one control system has not been explored. Therefore, this paper proposes a decentralized multi-functional virtual impedance (MFVI) scheme for AC islanded microgrids that can enhance the accuracy of reactive power sharing during normal conditions and limit the fault current of inverter-based DGs during faults using adaptive multi-functional characteristics depending on the output current and voltage of the DGs. In addition, the control scheme is provided with negative sequence (NS) inner control loops to mitigate the voltage unbalance in unbalanced microgrids during normal conditions. The MFVI control scheme was tested on the IEEE 13-bus system. The results show that the proposed scheme enhances the reactive power sharing during normal loading conditions and provides DG fault current limitation.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of an Optimized Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) Controller for Photovoltaic (PV) Based Microgrid in Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of the proposed Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller for photovoltaic with microgrid connected in power system. Conventional PI controller faced the problems of longer oscillation time, higher amplitude, higher overshoot, and the presence of steady-state error in PV-based microgrids during fault conditions. Hence, the objectives are to introduce and analyze the role of an optimized PID controller in a PV microgrid connected, contributing to faster response techniques that enhance system's stability during faults, including DC and AC faults, and to improve the system's steadiness and reliability. The proposed controller has been designed to ensure the stability of current regulations during outages that might be caused by unsymmetrical faults which considering scenario with high and low load demands, as well as varying transmission line length. A PI controller is utilized within the current regulator while gains of the DC/DC booster are tuned to stabilize the current during outages in both DC and AC faults by applying try-and-error method. Comprehensive and comparative stability analyses are conducted using bode plots and pole-zero mapping techniques in MATLAB/Simulink software to validate the system's stability based on the PI controller parameters. The optimized PID controller's performance used comparative analysis with a conventional PID controller under specific scenarios. The proposed controller shows a positive result towards the research hence the design of system, tuning method, and analytical result to validate the result under unsymmetrical fault condition and other circumstance is being presented.

articleTitle: Validating IP Reputation in Cloud Firewall Systems Using Machine Learning Driven Signature Generation and Detection Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper offers a new approach to validation for IP address reputation (IPR) using dynamic signatures achieved through the application of machine learning (ML) to conduct an accurate detection of malicious IPs. The proposed solution connects to the Amazon Web Services (AWS) Web Application Firewall (WAF) to improve security by deploying artificial intelligence (AI) models and natural language (NL) processing for automation of information extraction from IP-related information saved in the AWS object storages. All these lead to minimization of the number of false positives, real-time feedback, and optimization of IP reputation checking. The experimental outcome proves the capability of the proposed system to mitigate the IP address of the attacker and improve the protection of web applications against cybercrimes. This new approach is much advanced and a major leap ahead of other conventional IP reputation techniques, which offer a good protection shield against spam, DDoS, and other such evils.

articleTitle: Design of an Extended State Cubature Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper explores the filtering problem of a nonlinear system characterized by linear measurement equations and subjected to unknown disturbances and measurement noise. Inspired by the extended-state observer (ESO), an extended-state cubature Kalman filter (ESCKF) is proposed to simultaneously estimate disturbances, uncertainties, and filter noise generated during sensor measurements. It is demonstrated, under certain conditions, that the observation error of this filter converges. ESCKF employs the filtered system state values a s t he input f or t he controller and compensates for the estimated disturbances within the controller, enhancing control accuracy and enabling the system to operate effectively in challenging environments. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, simulations are performed using the MATLAB/Simulink software with a bridge crane system as the model. By comparing the control output waveforms and performance indicators related to the bridge crane system with those of other methods, the method reveals superior performance in the estimation of disturbances and noise attenuation.

articleTitle: Adaptive Droop-Based Differential Current Protection Scheme for Inverter-Based Islanded Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The fault current limitation embedded in the current controller of inverter-based distributed generators (IBDGs) in islanded microgrids poses a significant challenge for microgrid protection. This paper presents a novel adaptive droop-based protection scheme for islanded microgrids supplied by IBDGs. During fault conditions, one or more IBDGs can adaptively adjust their droop settings by modifying the no-load frequency limit (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">NL</inf>), resulting in different frequencies across the distributed generators. To achieve this adjustment, the droop-based controller of the selected IBDGs is enhanced with a unique positive sequence voltage versus no-load frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{I \ BDG}^{+}-f_{NL})$</tex> droop. These modifications result in different frequency current components at both terminals of the faulted line that aid in fault detection. The effectiveness of the proposed scheme is evaluated using a modified IEEE 33-bus islanded microgrid modeled in PSCAD/EMTDC, demonstrating its ability to detect and isolate faults in the inverter-based islanded microgrid. The simulation results show that the proposed adaptive droop-based protection scheme can accurately distinguish between normal and faulty conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Flyback Converter's Primary Current at High Switching Frequency Utilizing Novel Input Impedance Match Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The isolation capabilities of the flyback-based converter have garnered significant attention in different applications, particularly in photovoltaic inverter systems. However, the behavior of the anomalies, especially the parasitic element, has posed a significant difficulty in design. These irregularities ultimately interfere with the switching sequence, particularly during the current peak control operation. A novel topology is suggested to address the issue of distorted primary current during current peak control operation by leveraging the relationship between inductance and frequency in the parallel resonant circuit, as well as the input impedance of the converter. For this reason, an adaptive auxiliary path is activated during high-frequency switching. Analysis of acquiring the critical component value using the proposed input impedance match is discussed, and the alleviated result from the 100W enhanced converter topology test bench is obtained and presented.

articleTitle: CBF-DOB-Based Current-Constrained Control for PMSM Systems Subject to Unmatched Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This article addresses the speed regulation problem of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with overcurrent protection and time-varying disturbances. A novel safety-critical robust control algorithm is developed with control barrier function (CBF) and disturbance observers (DOBs). Two disturbance observers are first utilized to estimate lumped disturbances caused by external load torques and parameter uncertainties. Then, a safety-related CBF with disturbance compensation mechanism is designed to guarantee the overcurrent protection and robust performance of PMSM. Finally, the CBF-DOB based safe controller can be obtained by solving a quadratic program (QP) with the sliding mode control (SMC) integrated as a nominal controller. Numerical examples are extensively conducted to demonstrate the promising benefits of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Impact Assessment of Distributed Secondary Control Schemes for Autonomous AC Microgrids Under Multipoint FDI Attacks on Q-V Droop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Following the gradual maturity of the autonomous AC microgrid technology, the security and robustness of power electronic-based distributed energy resources are becoming increasingly important. Cyberattack on the microgrid hierarchical control layers is a growing concern. In this paper, the impacts of False Data Injection (FDI) cyber-attacks onto the secondary control layer that is comprised of the well-established distributed consensus control schemes, i.e., distributed dispatch control and distributed virtual output impedance (VOI) control, are compressively assessed respectively. The assessment focuses on FDI attacks on the Q-V droop structure, which is rarely investigated to date. The analysis is benchmarked against the centralized control scheme. All the considered schemes shared to the widest possible extent the same inner voltage and current control loops, thereby improving the validity of comparison and discussion. Disturbances of the point of common coupling's phase voltage magnitude and reactive power are discussed, and the relative resilience of the considered secondary control schemes is drawn, providing evidence to support the development of a resilient AC microgrid system.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Large Signal Stability Analysis of Dispatchable Virtual Oscillator Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Large-signal stability is a crucial aspect of power system planning, mainly concerning the ability of power sources to re-synchronize with each other following a disturbance. This paper delves into an exhaustive examination of the large-signal stability under dispatchable virtual oscillator control (DVOC), a sophisticated grid-forming control paradigm meticulously de-signed to facilitate the seamless integration of renewable energy sources into forthcoming grid infrastructures. Commencing with a detailed characterization of power transfer dynamics between DVOC and the grid, the study proceeds to derive the critical clearing time, serving as a pivotal metric delineating the maximum permissible fault duration before system stability is compromised. Employing both Lyapunov's indirect and direct methods and supported by an innovative nonlinear Lyapunov function, the analysis intricately navigates stability and attraction domains, thereby elucidating the salient parameters governing large-signal stability under DVOC. Rigorous validation of the proposed critical clearing time and Lyapunov function is es-tablished through comprehensive simulations executed within MATLAB/Simulink, affirming their technical robustness and practical applicability across diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Online Trajectory Planning for Adaptive Battery Discharging in Fuel Cell Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: This paper presents an online trajectory planning approach for optimal coordination of Fuel Cell (FC) and battery in plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (HEV). One of the main challenges in energy management of plug-in HEV is generating State-of-Charge (SOC) reference curves by optimally depleting battery under high uncertainties in driving scenarios. Recent studies have begun to explore the potential of utilizing partial trip information for optimal SOC trajectory planning, but dynamic responses of the FC system are not taken into account. On the other hand, research focusing on dynamic operation of FC systems often focuses on air flow management, and battery has been treated only partially. Our aim is to fill this gap by designing an online trajectory planner for dynamic coordination of FC and battery systems that works with a high-level SOC planner in a hierarchical manner. We propose an iterative LQR based online trajectory planning method where the amount of electricity dischargeable at each driving segment can be explicitly and adaptively specified by the high-level planner. Numerical results are provided as a proof of concept example to show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Application of Artificial Intelligence Techniques to Enhance the Solar Power Generation: Case Study in Sri Lanka
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The increasing energy demand, high fuel import cost, air pollution and global warming are indicating the need of elimination of fossil fuels and it also have heightened the quest for cleaner and renewable energy sources. Even though the unique climatic and geographic characteristics of Sri Lanka pose opportunities for solar power generation, the country is struggling to optimize the full potential of solar power resource due to the less technological involvement. Since solar energy variable with the unpredictability of nature, determining the future solar power generation in advance which is called solar forecasting will give the solar energy sector with a great advantage. The previous studies used machine learning algorithms to anticipate the solar power that have shown greater results than traditional forecasting methods. This research involves the impact of solar module temperature in solar panel efficiency and the implementation of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model for solar module temperature prediction. By using the predicted module temperature and other environmental parameters such as solar irradiance, windspeed and ambient temperature, the LSTM model can predict the accurate solar power forecasting for one day time horizon. Experimental results show the difference in accuracy level when using the predicted module temperature for forecasting than using actual module temperature.

articleTitle: AI-Based Surrogate Models of Digital Twins for Industrial Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Digital twins represent virtual replicas of physical systems, integrating real-time data and advanced analytics to monitor, simulate, and optimize industrial processes. This research delves into the application of AI-based surrogate models to improve the efficiency and accuracy of digital twins for industrial processes. The study employs machine learning techniques to develop computationally efficient models that maintain high accuracy. The integration of advanced sampling techniques and challenges related to data quality and interpretability are highlighted, proposing solutions to improve model robustness and reliability.

articleTitle: Optimizing Solar PV System Performance Using Feedforward Neural Network Control Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) are important in solar energy applications as a way to improve the efficiency of solar energy systems by overcoming the limitations of traditional Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) techniques. This paper will introduce Feedforward Neural Network (FNN) as the control algorithm to make the solar PV system in a specific residential village at Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS (UTP) more effective. The algorithm will aim at optimizing energy generation and improving system efficiency through a dynamic adjustment of boost converter pulse width modulation (PWM) duty cycle. The MATLAB Simulink software platform is used to develop and analyze a FNN control algorithm. Using MATLAB, a simulation of the photovoltaic (PV) system is created and simulated to supply sufficient power for the residential village at UTP. The result of this study shows that FNN control algorithm is effective in maximizing output power of PV systems by adjusting the PWM signal controlling the boost converter and is comparable to common MPPT methods such as Perturb and Observe (P&O) algorithm. Future work includes fine-tuning the hyperparameters of FNN, incorporation of additional features through feature engineering and the application of regularization techniques.

articleTitle: Advancement in High-Power Fast Charging Technologies for Electric Vehicles: Converter Topologies, Control Methods, and Infrastructure Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Industrial Electronics and Applications Conference (IEACon)
abstract: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) necessitates advancements in battery charging technologies to address concerns related to charging time, efficiency, and infrastructure integration. This paper explores the latest developments in high-power fast charging technologies, focusing on converter topologies, control methods, and their integration into existing power grids and renewable energy sources. Key innovations such as Boost, Cuk, SEPIC, Zeta, and Luo converters, as well as partial-power converters (PPC) and bidirectional Vienna rectifiers, are analyzed for their efficiency and suitability in fast charging applications. The impact of fast charging on battery life and grid stability is examined, highlighting the need for advanced power management solutions and smart charging algorithms. Additionally, the integration of renewable energy sources into fast charging infrastructure is discussed as a sustainable approach to enhancing the overall efficiency and reliability of EV charging. Through a comprehensive review of current technologies and methodologies, this paper aims to provide insights into the future direction of EV fast charging systems, ensuring their role in supporting the widespread adoption of electric mobility.
